CausalChain: Tumor cells -> Secretion of EVs enriched in miR-155 -> Uptake of EVs by mature monocytes/neutrophils -> miR-155 downregulates IRF-8 expression -> Impaired differentiation into mature myeloid effector cells -> Acquisition of MDSC immunosuppressive phenotype -> Suppression of T cell immune responses -> Enhanced tumor immune evasion
Hypothesis: Tumor-derived EVs carrying miR-155 induce epigenetic suppression of IRF-8 in mature myeloid cells, steering their differentiation toward an MDSC phenotype; therefore, interrupting this EV-mediated delivery or restoring IRF-8 expression may reprogram MDSCs into functional antigen-presenting cells and improve immunotherapeutic outcomes.
Abstract: We propose that tumor‐derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), particularly those enriched in miR‐155, drive the epigenetic reprogramming of mature myeloid cells by downregulating IRF‐8, a master regulator of normal myelopoiesis. This EV‐mediated transfer of miR‐155 impairs differentiation of monocytes and neutrophils into mature immune effector cells and instead fosters their conversion into highly suppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). This new mechanism of immune evasion suggests that targeted disruption of EV cargo delivery or restoration of IRF‐8 expression in myeloid cells may counteract MDSC‐mediated immune suppression and thereby enhance antitumor responses in cancer patients.
